Infra map

How Bunkai TMS is built and the non-functional budgets it holds, reverse-engineered from the product code of upex-bunkai-tms at staging commit 98ee1b4 (read-only snapshot). Paths are relative to that repo. At that point the production branch main still sits at e88512e, an ancestor of staging: this map describes what staging runs, and the environments section says what that means for production. Phase 2 sections (architecture, external services, background jobs, NFRs) come first, then the Phase 3 sections (backend, frontend, environments, CI/CD). Design-time intent from the target .context/SRS/ is quoted only where labelled as intent: it is not evidence of implementation.

Overview

Bunkai is a single Next.js App Router application that serves both the web UI and a versioned REST API (app/api/v1/**, 120 route files, 160 handlers in the posture snapshot) from one Vercel deployable, backed by one Supabase project (Postgres with Row Level Security, Auth, Realtime, Storage, Vault and pg_cron). There is still no separate backend service, no ORM, no queue and no cache tier. Business rules live in Postgres functions (bunkai_* RPCs) and RLS; route handlers parse, authenticate, call one RPC or an RLS-checked query, and map errors. Work that outlives a request runs in Next.js after() callbacks (Jira import, workspace export, deletion emails), in four pg_cron jobs inside the database, and in two Vercel Cron calls. Three SaaS integrations: Stripe (plan upgrade, invoices, payment method), Resend (outbound email) and Jira Cloud (story import), the last one now configured per workspace with its token kept in Supabase Vault, not in an env key. The pattern is a modular monolith organised by domain under lib/ (runs and run evidence, bugs, billing, chat, saved views, tracker settings, storage, notifications, coverage, workspace export and deletion, and more), with app/ owning routing and pages. A first command-line client, apps/bunkai-cli, calls the public API only.

Containers and data flow

  • Browser → app: page requests pass the middleware (session refresh via getUser), then server components query Postgres with the user's JWT, so RLS decides what rows come back. Client components call /api/v1/* with fetch and the session cookie.
  • API client → app: Authorization: Bearer bk_pat_* (scripts, the bunkai CLI, agents, automated executors submitting runs). The gateway verifies the PAT, checks the route's scope, then mints a 60-second user JWT so Postgres sees the token owner exactly as for a browser call.
  • Vercel Cron → app: GET /api/v1/admin/send-digest daily at 08:00 UTC and GET /api/v1/admin/storage-cleanup daily at 03:00 UTC, both with Authorization: Bearer {CRON_SECRET}; registered from the production deployment only.
  • App → Supabase Auth: getUser on every matched request and again in the gateway for cookie calls; sign-up, password sign-in, OTP verify, OTP resend, magic link, OAuth authorize URL, admin user lookups.
  • App → Postgres: PostgREST over HTTPS through @supabase/supabase-js, either user-scoped (RLS applies) or service-role (RLS bypassed: PAT lookup, secret tables, rate-limit store, Jira credentials, invite acceptance, idempotency rows, webhook, cron routes, background workers).
  • App ↔ Storage: the export worker uploads the zip to workspace-exports; run and defect evidence goes straight from the browser to run-evidence through a signed upload URL (init, PUT, commit), and is read back through 60-second signed URLs minted after an RLS check. Evidence bytes never cross a Vercel function.
  • Realtime → browser: row changes on run_atcs, run_steps, notifications, chat_messages and bugs are pushed to subscribed browsers (RLS-filtered). Every channel joins with the user's JWT, never as anon (lib/supabase/realtime-auth.ts).
  • App ↔ Stripe: the app creates Checkout Sessions (plan upgrade and payment-method setup), lists and retrieves invoices, updates the customer; Stripe calls back POST /api/v1/billing/webhook (signature-verified) with checkout and invoice events.
  • App → Resend and Jira Cloud: the digest and deletion emails go out through Resend; the import worker pages Jira's /rest/api/3/search/jql with the workspace's own connection, and the settings checks call /rest/api/3/myself and the create-meta endpoint.
  • Inside Postgres: pg_cron runs the human-run sweep, the agent-run sweep, the deleted-workspace purge and the rate-limit sweep (background-jobs). The database makes no outbound calls (pg_net / http not installed, per business-data-context integration-supabase).

Auth flow

Four ways in, all ending in a Supabase user id (request detail in backend):

  1. Password (UI or headless): POST /api/v1/auth/check-email routes the form; POST /api/v1/auth/signup answers 202 pending_confirmation and Supabase emails a code; POST /api/v1/auth/confirm verifies the 6 to 8 digit code; POST /api/v1/auth/signin signs in. Confirm and sign-in set the sb-* cookies and return the session plus a PAT shown once. Check-email, sign-in and confirm are throttled per network source, sign-in and confirm also per account (429 rate_limited with Retry-After).
  2. Magic link: POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link (existing accounts only) → email → GET /auth/callback, which sets the session and redirects to next.
  3. OAuth: GET /auth/oauth/{github|google} sets a state cookie and redirects to the provider through Supabase; the callback rejects a state mismatch before exchanging the code.
  4. PAT on later calls: bk_pat_{12-char prefix}.{secret}, prefix lookup with the service-role client, SHA-256 compare, uniform 401 on any failure, scope check (403), 60-second user JWT for RLS.

Every handler declares one of four postures (public, authenticated, cookie-only, required with capabilities); a route without one does not compile, and lib/api/route-posture-scan.ts diffs every handler against the committed snapshot. Tier counts and refusal semantics are in business-api-context (auth-model).

Database at architecture level

One store: Supabase Postgres, reached through PostgREST (no ORM, no direct connection from the app). Subsystems by migration: tenancy, membership ladder and invites, projects and modules, authoring (stories, criteria, ATCs with archive, restore and bulk edit), test design (tests, test plans with close and reopen, milestones and their plans, tags, saved views), execution (runs, run snapshot, environments, automated submissions, step evidence, run compare, flakiness), bugs (with corrections and evidence), team chat, activity and notifications, reports (coverage, traceability, defect heat map, recovery cycle), billing (plans, effective plan and grace, checkout sessions, invoices, Stripe events), imports and workspace Jira connections, workspace export and deletion, access tokens and secret side-tables, the rate-limit store, the Storage cleanup outbox, QA inspector roles and test failpoints. Tables and lifecycles belong to business-data-context; generated types live in lib/types/supabase.ts.

Security architecture

  • AuthN: Supabase Auth JWT in sb-* cookies for browsers; PATs (SHA-256 stored, 12-char prefix in clear) for API callers; CRON_SECRET for both cron routes; Stripe signature for the webhook.
  • AuthZ: scopes enforced in the gateway (requireCapability), roles and tenancy enforced in Postgres (RLS and SECURITY DEFINER helpers; roles viewer < member < admin < owner).
  • Service-role bypass: the admin client skips RLS; handlers and workers that use it check authorization in code.
  • Secrets at rest: PAT, magic-link and invite secrets hashed in *_secrets tables revoked from client and QA roles; Jira API tokens encrypted in Supabase Vault, readable only by one service-role function.
  • Abuse control: a Postgres sliding-window limiter, shared by every function instance, on the pre-auth and credential endpoints.

Performance hooks

No cache layer. The only app-level limiter is the auth one above. Keyset pagination on the long lists (now including the tests list), Home, workspace runs and workspace bugs indexes, a GIN-indexed ATC search vector, revalidatePath after the ATC Server Actions, Cache-Control on the OpenAPI spec, evidence uploads that bypass the function body limit. Details in nfr-performance.

QA relevance

  • Test RLS as a first-class surface: cross-workspace reads and writes per role, through the cookie path and the PAT path.
  • Asynchronous outcomes (import, export, deletion email, digest, storage cleanup, Realtime updates) are asserted on the job row, the outbox row, the mailbox or the subscribed page, never on the HTTP answer.
  • Stripe and Resend need sandbox credentials per environment, and Jira a connection saved in the test workspace, or the related flows answer with their degraded mode (503, 409 jira_not_connected, failed digest row).
  • The auth throttle is shared state: a test suite that signs in many times from one runner can be refused with 429.
  • Selectors: data-testid covers most of the authenticated app (see frontend).

Degraded modes are designed in, not crashes: a missing Stripe key answers 503 payment_processor_unavailable with a generic message (the missing variable goes to the server log only); a missing Resend key marks the digest row failed and the deletion still happens without its email; a workspace with no Jira connection gets 409 conflict (details.reason = jira_not_connected) before any import job exists, and a rejected token fails the job with jira_unauthorized. CRON_SECRET stays the one hard requirement: any server module that imports lib/env.ts throws at boot without it.

Stripe webhook: an unknown checkout session answers 5xx so Stripe redelivers; an invoice event for a customer not known yet is retried for one hour, then dropped; event ids are deduplicated in the database. Jira: HTTP 429 is retried with a 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 second backoff (or Retry-After), then the job fails; the connection check gives up after 5 seconds. Workspace invites still send no email: the token and accept_url come back once in the response.

Key-name drift: .env.example no longer names ATLASSIAN_URL and the app no longer reads any ATLASSIAN_* key, but ATLASSIAN_EMAIL and ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN stay there for the boilerplate tooling. It still lacks NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, CRON_SECRET, the three Stripe keys and RESEND_DIGEST_FROM_EMAIL (the first two are declared in .env.core.schema). Not in package.json or code: Sentry, PostHog, Cloudflare R2.

Background jobs and asynchronous work

Nothing runs on a queue or a worker host. Work that outlives a request runs in three places, each with its own trigger, environment reach and failure mode. What each job means to the business is in business-data-context (automatic-processes); this section holds where it runs and how a tester reaches it.

No route sets maxDuration, so every after() worker runs inside the platform's default function time limit for the plan; an import or export that outruns it is cut off and its job stays queued. Expired idempotency_keys rows are now deleted only when the same key is reused (no sweep), and nothing removes expired export archives from workspace-exports: the cleanup outbox covers evidence objects only.

QA relevance: the four pg_cron jobs act on production rows too, so a staging test that seeds an abandoned run, a silent agent run or a deleted workspace is acting on the same database production reads. Assert a sweep by seeding a run past its threshold and waiting one tick (or calling the function as an inspector); assert the digest and the storage cleanup on staging with a manual POST, never by waiting for the cron.

Backend

The backend is the server half of the single Next.js app: Route Handlers under app/api/v1/**, two Server Actions, server components, after() workers, and Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Realtime, Storage, Vault) reached over HTTP. No separate service, no ORM, no Docker.

Local development setup

# 1. Install dependencies
bun install

# 2. Environment: .env.example is NOT sufficient on its own (see the table above)
cp .env.example .env
#    then set at least:
#    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY,
#    SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, CRON_SECRET, SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET
#    optional per feature: STRIPE_*, RESEND_API_KEY
#    (Jira is connected per workspace in Settings > Jira, not through .env)

# 3. Database: no local Supabase stack and no migrate/seed command in the repo.
#    The keys point at the one shared Supabase project (production data lives there too).
#    Optional, after a schema change on that project:
bun run types:gen

# 4. Start the dev server (http://localhost:3000)
bun run dev

# 5. Verify (liveness only, does not touch the database)
curl http://localhost:3000/api/v1/health

# Build and serve like production
bun run build
bun run start

Test and quality commands

395 product test files (app/, lib/, components/, apps/ and middleware.test.ts) run with bun test. 99 of them read live Supabase credentials (service key, JWT secret or the QA_E2E_USER_* account) and skip themselves when they are missing, so a run without credentials passes without exercising the database. With credentials they create and delete their own rows and users in the shared Supabase project. No git hook and no CI runs them (ci-cd). 

bun test            # or: bun run test:guarded
bun run typecheck
bun run lint:check
bun run openapi:check

Auth flow (the contract tests must speak)

PathRequestSuccessCredential producedFound in
Email lookupPOST /api/v1/auth/check-email { email }200 { exists, confirmed }; 429 rate_limited past 10 per 60 s or 60 per hour from one sourcenone (routes the login form)app/api/v1/auth/check-email/route.ts
Sign-upPOST /api/v1/auth/signup { email, password } (password 8 characters to 72 bytes)202 { status: "pending_confirmation", email }; Supabase emails a code. 409 for an existing address; 422 for a reserved domain (example.com, .test, ...)none yetapp/api/v1/auth/signup/route.ts, lib/auth/password-policy.ts, lib/auth/reserved-email-domain.ts
ConfirmPOST /api/v1/auth/confirm { email, token, pat_name?, pat_scopes?, pat_expires_in_days? } (token 6 to 8 digits)200, same body as sign-in; uniform 401; 429 per source or per accountsb-* cookies + session tokens + PATapp/api/v1/auth/confirm/route.ts
Resend codePOST /api/v1/auth/resend202 { status: "sent", email }, whether or not the address existsnoneapp/api/v1/auth/resend/route.ts
Sign-inPOST /api/v1/auth/signin { email, password, pat_name?, pat_scopes?, pat_expires_in_days? } (password 6 to 128)200; uniform 401 "Invalid email or password."; 403 if workspace:admin is requested; 429 past 10 per 60 s per source or 10 per 15 min per accountsb-* cookies + session tokens + PAT (default scopes atc:read, atc:write, run:execute)app/api/v1/auth/signin/route.ts, lib/api/pat.ts, lib/auth/rate-limit.ts
Magic linkPOST /api/v1/auth/magic-link { email, next? }200 { ok: true } also for unknown emails; the link lands on GET /auth/callbacksb-* cookies, redirect to nextapp/api/v1/auth/magic-link/route.ts, app/auth/callback/route.ts
OAuthGET /auth/oauth/{github|google}?next=…302 to the provider, back to /auth/callbacksb-* cookiesapp/auth/oauth/[provider]/route.ts
PAT from a sessionPOST /api/v1/tokens { scopes, name?, workspace_id?, expires_in_days? } with the session cookie201; a PAT gets 403 herePAT (any scope subset; workspace:admin needs workspace_id and admin or owner role)app/api/v1/tokens/route.ts
API call with PATAuthorization: Bearer bk_pat_{12-char prefix}.{rest}Accepted by every non-cookie-only handler whose scope the token holds-lib/api/principal.ts, lib/api/middleware/bearer.ts
 
# Sign-in / confirm response body (200)
{ "user": { "id": "<uuid>", "email": "..." },
  "session": { "access_token", "refresh_token", "expires_at", "token_type" },
  "pat": { "token": "bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>", "id", "name", "scopes", "expires_at" },
  "warning": "Store the PAT token now — it cannot be retrieved later." }
# plus Set-Cookie: sb-<project-ref>-auth-token... (Supabase SSR cookies)
  • Sign-up does not create a confirmed user or mint a PAT: a new test identity needs the emailed code, so headless provisioning needs a readable inbox or a pre-provisioned account (the product team uses QA_E2E_USER_*).
  • Sign-in is throttled per network source and per account. The source is the address Vercel asserts; locally, with no Vercel header, every caller shares one unknown bucket.
  • The Supabase access_token is not accepted as a Bearer: only bk_pat_ tokens are.
  • A Bearer header wins over a cookie on the same request.
  • The session cookie name embeds the Supabase project ref; with one shared project it is the same name on every environment, but cookies are scoped to the app's own host.
  • Health: GET /api/v1/health (liveness, no DB). Discovery banner: GET /api/v1. Spec: GET /api/openapi, whose paths carry the full /api/v1/… prefix and whose servers are bare hosts.

Test-architecture decisions built on this contract: ADR-0009 and ADR-0010 in this QA repo (both Accepted). ADR-0009's per-run sign-in now has to fit the sign-in throttle (see discovery-gaps).

Rendering model

  • React Server Components for authenticated pages under app/(app)/: they read Supabase with the cookie session (RLS applies).
  • Client components for interactive parts; they call /api/v1/* with fetch and the session cookie. Evidence images go from the browser straight to Storage through a signed upload URL.
  • Live updates: the run page (components/runs/RunnerView.tsx), the sidebar inbox (components/layout/AppSidebar.tsx), the team chat (components/chat/ChatPanel.tsx) and the bug heat map (components/bugs/BugsHeatmapView.tsx) subscribe to Supabase Realtime channels, each joined with the user token first.
  • Team chat is a dock mounted by the authenticated layout on every (app) page.
  • Two Server Actions, both followed by revalidatePath.
  • Middleware redirects anonymous users from /home, /projects, /onboarding, /settings, /activity, /atcs and /workspaces, except /workspaces/{id}/restore. / redirects to /login.
  • Theme is dark only (dark class fixed on the root element; sonner Toaster with theme="dark").
  • Route-level loading states exist only for run compare and the tests list (loading.tsx); no error.tsx.

Styling and component library

  • Tailwind CSS 3 with CSS-variable design tokens (tailwind.config.ts, app/globals.css); spec in DESIGN.md.
  • shadcn/ui configuration (components.json); primitives in components/ui/: badge, button, card, input, label, meter, select, switch, tabs. Radix dialog, dropdown-menu, tabs, tooltip.
  • Feature libraries: TanStack Table, Monaco via next/dynamic, cmdk, sonner, dnd-kit (drag-and-drop reordering of tests), react-markdown + remark-gfm + rehype-sanitize; shiki only on /qa.
  • Fonts: Inter, JetBrains Mono, Noto Serif JP via next/font/google.

State, data fetching and auth integration

  • No global store and no fetching library: server components query Supabase, client components use fetch + useState, React context providers for chat, plus Realtime subscriptions. Workbench filters are written into the address bar (debounced history.replaceState), and named saved views are stored per project through /api/v1/projects/{id}/saved-views (lib/saved-views/).
  • AuthProvider (components/providers/auth-context.tsx) tracks the Supabase session on the browser client.
  • Active workspace persists in the bk_active_ws cookie, switched through POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace.
  • Client env vars: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (and NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, read server-side only). No secret-looking name carries the public prefix.

Static assets and SEO

public/ holds openapi.json and qa/supabase-root-2021-ca.crt (for the QA database connection): no favicon, robots.txt or sitemap. No next/image usage. Root metadata sets the title and a metadataBase hard-coded to http://localhost:3000 in every environment. Bundle size is not measured (see nfr-performance).

Test-ID strategy

  • data-testid is the de facto selector contract: 1,028 distinct static values across 149 non-test component and page files, covering every feature area including chat, saved views, tracker settings, run compare, evidence upload and billing details.
  • Naming is mostly kebab-case with an area prefix (home-*, bug-*, runner-*, traceability-*), with a few outliers in camelCase or snake_case (for example notificationRow, notification_unread_dot); dynamic ids are built with template literals.
  • aria-* attributes are widespread in app and components, so role and accessible-name locators work alongside the test ids.
  • Component tests in the product use @happy-dom/global-registrator (for example components/billing/BillingOverviewView.test.ts).

Internationalization

None: no i18n library, lang="en" on the root element, English strings hard-coded. Only the /qa guide content is Spanish.

Install and run

bun install
bun run dev     # http://localhost:3000 → redirects to /login
bun run build
bun run start

Environments

The app decides its environment from Vercel's VERCEL_ENV and maps it to a hard-coded URL table (lib/urls.ts APP_URLS, also the OpenAPI servers). The product repo's own .agents/project.yaml names the branches (main = production, staging = integration, release by fast-forward promotion) and still declares one Supabase project for all environments during the MVP. This QA repo declares local and staging under environments: in .agents/project.yaml.

A staging test writes into the database production reads.

Monitoring and rollback

  • Monitoring: the JSON access log on stdout (Vercel function logs), job and outbox rows in the database and cron.job_run_details. No error tracking, uptime monitor or APM (nfr-observability).
  • Rollback: app code through Vercel (redeploy a previous deployment); main moves only by fast-forward, so a code rollback is a revert commit. Schema changes are forward-only with no down scripts and land on the one shared database, so a DB rollback needs a hand-written reverse migration or a Supabase backup restore affecting every environment.

QA relevance

  • Run against staging by default; never write to production. With one shared Supabase project, "staging data" is a convention (own users and workspaces), not an isolation boundary.
  • Production is behind staging by the whole feature set added since e88512e: a regression run against production tests a different product.
  • Auth cookies carry the shared project ref, but are host-scoped, so a storageState from one host does not apply to another.
  • Email links use APP_URLS, not the request host: a test on a preview or a non-3000 local port follows links to another host.
  • Rate-limit buckets are shared across environments: sign-in attempts against staging count toward the same per-account budget a local run uses.
  • A Jira import test needs a Jira connection saved on the test workspace; there is no deployment-wide fallback.

CI/CD

CI pipelines

None in the repo, and none in its history: no .github/, .gitlab-ci.yml or other CI config. The product's 395 test files run only when a developer runs bun test. The automated gates are local git hooks (husky), skippable with --no-verify, and none runs the tests. The hooks now source a synced .husky/framework-gates.sh and keep the product's own OpenAPI gate around that call:

HookRuns
pre-commitbunx lint-staged (eslint --fix, prettier --write); framework gates: types:check, vars:check, skills:check, and conditionally skills:registry:check, agents:schema:check, vars:schema:check, instructions:check, agents:compat:check by staged path; then openapi:check when a route.openapi.ts, lib/openapi/, scripts/openapi-gen.ts or public/openapi.json is staged
pre-pushFramework gates: format:check, lint:check, vars:env:check (drift as warning), skills:registry:check, agents:compat:check, docs:check, the documentation-contract lint and a varlock warning; then bun scripts/openapi-gen.ts --check
commit-msgForensic-trailer check, warn-only, never blocks

Of those, lint, prettier, tsc and the OpenAPI freshness check touch the product; the rest checks the inherited boilerplate. The OpenAPI spec cannot drift from the routes silently (both hooks check it).

Deployment

  • Target: Vercel. Branch model from the product .agents/project.yaml: feature branches merge into staging by --no-ff PR; a release fast-forwards main to staging; hotfixes branch off main and back-merge the same day. main and staging are protected.
  • vercel.json holds only the two cron entries; build, install and output settings are Vercel's Next.js defaults or live in the dashboard. Whether the git integration deploys each branch automatically is inferred, not verified.
  • Release gate: bun run release:check runs the executable checks in .context/release/pending-production-v2.md, which still lists the same five pending entries for the v2 promotion (stateless magic-link switch, auth email rate limit, confirmation email copy, release tag and version, Supabase config snapshot). The repo has no release tag yet.
  • No Dockerfile, Compose file or other host config.

Database migrations

No pipeline: migrations are applied by hand (or by an agent) to the one Supabase project through the Supabase MCP apply_migration tool, which writes one ledger row per file; supabase/migrations/README.md holds the convention and a repair log (several amended re-applies collapsed back to one row). Because the project is shared, a migration reaches production's database the moment it is applied for staging, before the matching code is promoted.

Infrastructure as code

Not present (no Terraform, Pulumi, CDK or Serverless files; no Supabase config snapshot).

Deployment checklist (derived; only the release ledger is enforced, by command)

  • Pre-deploy: bun test with live credentials, bun run typecheck, bun run lint:check, bun run openapi:check, bun run release:check exit 0; migrations backward-compatible with the code still on main.
  • Post-deploy: GET /api/v1/health answers ok; /login renders; a headless signin returns 200; vercel crons list shows the digest and the storage cleanup after the first production deploy that carries vercel.json.
  • Rollback: redeploy the previous Vercel deployment; reverse migrations by hand (see environments).

QA relevance

  • This QA repo's own CI would be the first automated test job against the product; nothing links a product deploy to a QA run, so regression runs are triggered by hand or on schedule.
  • Staging changes with every merge (620 commits on staging since 2026-10-13); correlate a failure with the staging branch log, since there is no deploy log in the repo.
  • The product's live-database tests and this QA repo's tests write into the same Supabase project and spend the same rate-limit buckets; coordinate data naming, cleanup and sign-in volume.
  • The product now accepts automated results (POST /api/v1/runs/submissions, streamed step marks), so a CI job could report into Bunkai itself; nothing in either repo does so yet.

Discovery gaps

  • Snapshot scope: refreshed from origin/staging 4ccd8ed (2026-11-17) read through git, against the earlier 98ee1b4 baseline; nothing was deployed, called or measured. origin/main = e88512e is as of the local repo's last fetch.
  • Shared Supabase project: declared by the product team (one project for local, staging, production). Whether production's database really carries all 131 migrations while serving e88512e code, and whether that old code still works against the newer schema, was not verified. Source: Supabase project owner.
  • Production branch lag: main is 1,662 commits behind staging; when v2 will be promoted is a release decision outside the repo.
  • Cron routes: the digest (08:00 UTC) and the storage cleanup (03:00 UTC) are registered from production only, and production has no vercel.json yet, so neither runs anywhere on a schedule; evidence objects queued for deletion on the shared project wait for a manual POST. The presence of CRON_SECRET on staging was not checked.
  • Magic-link rail: the code still sends PKCE links (app/api/v1/auth/magic-link/route.ts); the stateless token_hash rail in /auth/callback is built but not switched on (release ledger BK-400, still pending). business-api-context auth-cookie-session describes the stateless rail as live: that contradicts the code.
  • Sign-in throttle versus test login: since 2026-11-13 sign-in and confirm allow 10 attempts per 60 s per source and 10 per 15 min per account (lib/auth/rate-limit.ts). QA ADR-0009 mints fresh credentials on every Playwright run and lists "no rate limit" as a consequence; how many sign-ins one run makes per role account, and whether CI and local runs share a budget, is not recorded in the ADR. Source: this repo's setup files and ADR owner.
  • Rate-limit source in CI: the limiter trusts only Vercel's client-address headers; a QA runner behind a NAT or a shared CI egress puts every parallel worker in one source bucket. Not measured.
  • Performance numbers: no latency, throughput or bundle-size measurement exists; SRS budgets are intent only.
  • Function time limit: no maxDuration; the Vercel plan's default limit for after() imports and exports is unknown. Source: Vercel project settings.
  • Background cleanup: expired idempotency_keys rows are removed only when the same key is reused, and expired export archives in workspace-exports are never removed (the cleanup outbox covers evidence only); confirm whether intended.
  • Accessibility: SRS targets WCAG 2.1 AA; not verified from code.
  • Selector convention: data-testid is widespread but not uniformly kebab-case; whether the team treats it as a contract (and will fix outliers) is a team decision.
  • Data cleanup: workspaces can be deleted (30-day purge) and members removed, but no API deletes a user; how QA users accumulating in the shared project are purged is undecided.
  • Test failpoints on the shared database: bunkai_test_failpoints lets a service-role caller force member removal or a workspace deletion request to fail. A failpoint row is read by the same RPCs production calls; how rows are scoped to a test's own workspace, and whether this QA repo may use the table, was not checked. Source: product ADR-0022 and its owner.
  • Supabase project settings: SMTP provider, templates, JWT expiry, password policy, Storage quota and backups live in the dashboard with no snapshot in git (ledger INFRA-GAP). Source: Supabase project owner.
  • Integration accounts: Stripe mode and webhook registration (now also invoice events), Resend sending domain, OAuth app settings, and which workspaces hold a Jira connection, live outside the repo and were not verified.
  • Unused schema: feature_flags still has no caller in app/, lib/ or components/ at 4ccd8ed; confirm whether it is planned or dead. (user_view_state is now read by saved views.)
  • Monaco CDN: the editor's runtime asset source is inferred from the library default, not observed.
  • API contract drift: the served spec now has 155 operations; this QA repo's synced api/openapi.json holds 144, so bun run api:sync is due. The served spec and .context/SRS/api-contracts.yaml were not compared (business-api-context discovery-gaps).
  • Diagram: no .diagram-design marker at the QA repo root; the figure keeps diagram-design's default skin. Its labels still show the 2026-10-13 counts (107 handlers, one 08:00 cron) and omit the second cron, Vault and the evidence bucket: a redraw is pending.
  • Runtime version: no Node.js version pinned; the version Vercel builds with is unknown. Source: Vercel project settings.
  • Local bootstrap: .env.example still lacks NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, CRON_SECRET, the Stripe keys and RESEND_DIGEST_FROM_EMAIL (the first two are now in .env.core.schema), so a fresh clone does not boot from it. Source: target maintainers.
  • Deploy mechanics: automatic deploys per branch and per-PR previews are inferred, not verified. Source: Vercel project settings.
  • Production liveness: https://upexbunkai.vercel.app was not contacted.
  • Hard-coded URLs: three URL sources (APP_URLS, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, request origin) and a localhost metadataBase; confirm intent before testing previews, a non-default local port or Stripe return URLs.
  • API base path for the test client: the OpenAPI servers are bare hosts with /api/v1/… paths, environments.*.api_url in .agents/project.yaml ends in /api, and the /qa guide uses /api/v1. /test-framework-adaptation must pick one convention.
  • CI, monitoring: no CI and no monitoring beyond stdout logs, job and outbox rows exist in the repo; confirm whether any live outside it. Source: target maintainers.
  • Inspector roles: created by migration 0085 and made loginable by db:qa-roles; their state on the shared project was not checked, and DB-level checks through them cannot prove RLS behaviour.
